quote.translation: "In this sense it is true to say that chance governs the world, or rather that chance has a part, and a notable part, in the governance of the world" (Il est vrai de dire en ce sens que le hasard gouverne le monde, ou plutôt qu'il a une part, et une part notable, dans le gouvernement du monde.)
(Cournot, Essai sur les fondements de nos connaissances, nouvelle édition, p. 47).
We have thought of chance as the apex at which indifference intersects with indifference.

regions.text: 我々は偶然どは無開心と無開心との交叉する尖端であると考へた。

quote.translation: To acknowledge the indifference of chance in the strict sense is, consequently, the ground on which we admit the objectivity of chance.

regions.text: 偶然の無開心性を嚴密なる意味に於て承認することが、偶然の客親性を許容する所以である。第二にたとへ交叉點が因果性の開心によつて裔らされた交叉點であると假定してもその交叉踏の完全なる釋明と十全なる認識とは單に理念に過ぎないことを思はなければならぬ。交叉踏を規定する因果系列は實に無敷にある。

quote.translation: Second, even if we suppose that a point of intersection has been brought about by the concern of causality, we must bear in mind that a complete explanation and an adequate knowledge of that point of intersection are merely an idea, for the causal series that determine a point of intersection are in fact innumerable.

quote.translation: E. 2), he does so on the basis of the innumerability of the causal series that converge on the point of intersection and, connected with this, the innumerability of the points of intersection themselves.

regions.text: ライプニッツが「偶然眞理」に開して「際限なき細目』（detailsansbornes）か「無限』（infinite）～か云つてるる（Leibniz,Monadologie,36）のも同様

quote.translation: When Leibniz speaks, concerning contingent truths, of "detail without bounds" (détail sans bornes) and of "the infinite" (infinité) (Leibniz, Monadologie, 36), it is for the same reason.
